title.narrative: Yemen Integrated Urban Services Emergency Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Integrated Urban Services Emergency Project for Yemen is to restore access to critical urban services in selected cities within the Republic of Yemen. The project financing is an IDA grant of SDR 106.2 million, in an amount equivalent to US 150 million dollars. The project will finance activities that support the restoration of critical urban services in selected Yemeni cities. The restoration of urban services, including water and sanitation, transport, energy and solid waste management, will be critical to improve health outcomes, basic living conditions and local economic activity. The project adopts an integrated approach to urban service delivery that provides coordinated, multi-sectoral support to Yemen during the conflict. The project has three components. First component, service restoration will support the restoration of critical urban services in selected cities in Yemen. The targeted services cover five sectors: tertiary municipal services and solid waste management, urban water and sanitation, urban roads, electricity for critical services, and housing. The project will focus on critical investments that can restore services in a short implementation timeframe. This component will finance works, goods, consultants services, non-consultant services, training, and operating costs of the local partners involved in the different subcomponents. All civil works under the project are expected to be undertaken by private sector contractors, thus supporting the revitalization of local economic activity. Second component, implementation support and capacity development will support capacity building activities for the stakeholders who will be involved in the delivery of activities under the project at central and local levels. These activities will focus on technical skills for all sectors involved in the project, including more effective human resource management, coordination, transparency and accountability, safeguards, and public financial management. Third component, contingent emergency response is to improve the country's response capacity in the event of an emergency, following the procedures governed by paragraph 12, Section III of the Bank Policy, Investment Project Financing. There is a possibility that, during project implementation, a natural disaster, epidemic or another emergency may occur, which would cause a major adverse economic and/or social impact.
To restore access to critical urban services in selected cities within the Republic of Yemen.

condition.narrative: The Recipient shall not later than December 31, 2017, prepare and adopt the Project Operational Manual, in form and substancesatisfactory to the Association.

The Recipient shall, within sixty (60) days from the Effective Date: (i) prepare, in accordance with terms of reference acceptableto the Association, an Environmental and Social Management Framework (“ESMF”), and a Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF),respectively, as well as any environmental assessment, environmental management plan or similar safeguard instrument required bythe ESMF, or any resettlement action plan required by the RPF, all in form and substance satisfactory to the Association; and(ii)adopt such ESMF and RPF as shall have been approved by the Association and publish said ESMF and RPF, and any environmentalassessment, environmental management plan or similar safeguard instrument, in a manner acceptable to the Association.

title.narrative: Cities in which beneficiary consultation informed activity prioritization

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Achievement of target: 100%.</strong> The Project pioneered and mainstreamed CE in urban services at the level of municipalities and communities. Citizens played a key role in identification, prioritization, and monitoring of investment projects under YIUSEP. This input helped validate priorities identified by the implementing agency and to choose between competing investment options. Feedback obtained from CE laid the foundation for positive, sustainable results to meet citizens’ needs.</p>
<p><strong>Achievement of target: 167%. </strong>Activities informed by women's participation in beneficiary consultations </p>

title.narrative: Energy generation supported through the Project

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Achievement of target: 178%</strong>. Project interventions resulted in 106,572 MWh of cumulative electricity generation. YIUSEP funded a total of 108 sub-projects in 10 cities with a total allocation of US$ 32,424,639. It successfully installed and rehabilitated solar PV-based electricity supply systems and diesel generators in 205 health and education facilities, and for 104 water wells in the target cities. In addition to the Rooftop Solar PV and Rental Power in hospitals, health facilities and schools, the interventions under this sub-component also included Solar LED Street Lights, indoor LED Bulbs and Solar Water heaters. The solar energy is more resilient, climate friendly and generates more jobs.</p>

<p><strong>Achievement of target: 105%.</strong> Project interventions resulted in reduction of 10,460 Tons of CO2 emissions exceeding the target of 10,000 tons.</p>

<p><strong>Achievement of target: 106%.</strong> Furthermore, these investments helped save 5,302 MWh of energy surpassing the end-target of 5,000 MWh. </p>

title.narrative: People provided access to rehabilitated water and sanitation services

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achievement of target: 100%</strong>. The Project successfully implemented a total of 74 sub-projects in 11 cities with a total allocation of US$22,378,495. It rehabilitated 113 water wells with a production of 1,879,200 m3/month; supplied and installed 8 large Solar PV systems for municipal water wells and 40 solar PV systems for rural communities’ water wells; provided 50 diesel generators; installed an analytical system for water quality control; rehabilitated 7.7 km of water network; provided 61 self-prime sewer pumps and 23 sewer vacuum trucks, which played critical role in flood response. In addition, it provided 110 ton of  emergency PPEs, safety equipment, hygiene and sterilization materials for Covid-19 response. These investments helped provide over 1.2 million people with access to rehabilitated water and sanitation services.</p>

<p><strong>Achievement of target: 112%.</strong> A total amount of US$ 37,310,530 was allocated to 146 sub-projects for tertiary municipal services in 8 cities. (a) In solid waste sector, a total of 7 landfill assessments were carried out and action plans produced for the cities of Sana'a, Aden, Mukalla, Dhamar, Sa'adah and Zinjibar.  The Project carried out 10 waste collection campaigns in these cities and successfully collected over 1 million cubic meters of accumulated waste, delivered service contracts to restore collection and transfer of solid waste to the landfill sites; developed environment and social safeguards mitigation measures for landfill sites; provided weighing stations for landfill sites and waste collection bins for the residents. ???????(b) YIUSEP has helped address urban flooding through investments in stormwater flood protection, through provision of box culverts, stormwater pumps and the suctioning of stagnant flood water from urban areas. It provided for rainwater/flood drainage in 5 districts of Amran, 2 districts of Sana'a, and 5 districts in Sa'adah. (c) The Project revamped local parks: 7 in Sana'a, 5 in Dhamar, 3 in Aden. It funded paved pathways, provided sitting spaces and shades, planted greenery, provided fncing, and created children’s play areas. The rehabilitation of local parks and green spaces provided a significant social benefit for the beneficiary communities. (d)  YIUSEP helped repair and expand sanitation network and its connection to treatment and disposal systems: 14 in Sana'a, 9 in Aden, 8 in Mukalla. It also repaired inspection chambers and manholes. (e) The project also made stone pavements in the neighborhood, particularly on pedestrian sidewalks. Stone pavements have been done in 19 districts in Aden, 16 in Sana'a, 14 districts in Mukalla, 5 each in Zinjibar and Dhamar, 3 in Al Dhale's, and 2 districts in Amran. </p>

title.narrative: Person-days of temporary employment created under the Project

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achievement of target: 107%.</strong> Throughout implementation the Project created around 1.6 million non-permanent person days for Yemeni workers in operating the infrastructure and equipment, thus supporting the revitalization of local economicactivity. This undoubtedly made a positive impact on highly stressed communities in Yemen and contributed to better operation of local businesses. </p>

<p><strong>Achievement of target: 111%. </strong>The Project rehabilitated 266 km of urban roads in the target cities exceeding thetarget of 240 km. A total of 45 subprojects were implemented in 8 cities with a total budget of about US$ 39,373,043. Three quarters of the interventions were carried out in Aden and Sana’a where roads were severely damaged due to the conflict. As a result,the repairs of asphalt roads, stone paving and streetlighting were commended by pedestrians, drivers, and shopkeepers alike. These interventions resulted in road safety, access to markets, and reduced car repairs. </p>

title.narrative: Beneficiaries with restored access to critical urban services

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achievement of target: 102%.</strong> The Project benefited the residents of the selected Yemen cities through restoring urban infrastructure, enhancing urban mobility and flood management, through citizen engagement activities with a high level of participation by women creating on-site job opportunities. The Project benefits also include outcome of institutional strengthening activities, which are key to planning and implementing similar activities in the future as well as ensuring their sustainability. The Project has achieved success in restoring and preserving basic services, sustaining institutional capacity, and building the foundations for shared and inclusive prosperity in a post-conflict environment.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of project financing executed by local contractors or suppliers

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achievement of target: 100%. </strong>During the life of the Project over 150 contracts were given to local suppliers and contractors, thus contributing to the local economy, which will trigger growth of local businesses. </p>
